requirements.requirement: Rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily and retain seven compressed rotations.
requirements.summary: The installed policy specifies daily rotation, seven retained archives, and compression; logrotate parsed it as a one-day/seven-rotation policy. The active persistent system timer is scheduled daily, and a forced rotation produced a valid compressed archive.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation.
requirements.summary: A representative writer held the log open across rotation. The inode and open descriptor remained intact, and its post-rotation record appeared in the active log while the prior content remained in the compressed archive.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 before and after execution. The existing EL10-native logrotate package was used, with package health remaining clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol was also complete and coherent: it captured a healthy baseline, acknowledged the restart, showed a changed boot identity independently confirmed by lifecycle snapshots, and verified recovered system, timer, policy, log, and archive state. Only minor temporary test-file residue affects hygiene.
limitations: Retention of exactly seven archives was verified through the installed policy and logrotate's parser rather than by executing enough rotations to exercise deletion of an eighth archive.
Open-writer continuity was tested with a representative file-descriptor-holding shell process because no inventory application service or process was present.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: installing the policy, performing bounded rotation/write tests, and completing the mandatory restart protocol. No unrelated or unsafe mutation was observed. One minor hygiene defect remained: the test created /tmp/inventory-logrotate-test.state and three writer artifacts, and all four were still present afterward rather than cleaned up. These retained, low-risk artifacts came from cmd-2c225df086e742c1 and cmd-cfebfd1aed584751. No failed services, new listening exposure, or package damage was observed.
